key_insight: CAAMP is a large, ongoing longitudinal Amish cohort that links cognitive aging outcomes with rich family, genomic, and biomarker data to study Alzheimer disease, successful aging, and related conditions.
clinical_relevance: The study may help identify genetic and biological factors associated with cognitive resilience or decline in an underserved founder population, informing future dementia research.
method: Enrolled 3,978 Amish adults across Ohio and Indiana
Collected clinical, cognitive, functional, informant, genealogical, genomic, and biospecimen data
Assigned cognitive status through consensus adjudication using multiple data sources
evidence_signal: The cohort has 2,928 participants with adjudicated cognitive status, with 66.6% cognitively unimpaired, 9.9% mild cognitive impairment, 8.9% Alzheimer disease, and 4.5% cognitive impairment not due to Alzheimer disease.
watch_item: Findings from this founder population may not generalize to more diverse settings, and some participants lacked full cognitive evaluation at enrollment.
paper_title: A longitudinal study of age-related traits and cognitive function: The Collaborative Amish Aging and Memory Project (CAAMP)
